section_context_en: SF-002 — Business scope and exclusions
raw_quote_en: The platform ingests enterprise documents and user-submitted cases, searches permitted knowledge, drafts grounded responses, applies deterministic risk policy, routes uncertain/sensitive recommendations to authorized reviewers, publishes through a satisfied gate, and preserves auditable evidence. Classification, retrieval, generation, policy evaluation, approval and publication are distinct activities; separate records do not require separate screens. [Source: pp.7,11–12, §§2.1–2.2; `screen_functions:r1:c4:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c11:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c13:f4`]
normalized_proposition_en: Classification, retrieval, generation, policy evaluation, approval and publication are distinct activities; separate records do not require separate screens.

section_context_en: SF-003 — Users, scopes and authorization prerequisites
raw_quote_en: Every request binds an authenticated principal and tenant. Authorization combines role, tenant, workspace membership, case sensitivity, source ACL, action and separation of duties. Apply checks at edge, domain transaction, retrieval, tool dispatch and publication as applicable; hiding or disabling navigation is not authorization. Originating ACL filtering precedes text release to generation. Cross-tenant resource substitution returns the absent-resource not-found response class without disclosing private existence. [Source: pp.21–23 §§5.1–5.3,34 chapter9,89 TST-003; `screen_functions:r1:c29:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c31:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c32:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c53:f2`, `screen_functions:r1:c141:f3`]
normalized_proposition_en: Apply checks at edge, domain transaction, retrieval, tool dispatch and publication as applicable; hiding or disabling navigation is not authorization.

section_context_en: SF-003 — Users, scopes and authorization prerequisites
raw_quote_en: Interactive authentication uses authorization-code flow with PKCE. Access tokens contain issuer, audience, expiry, subject and tenant; unexpected algorithms and missing tenancy claims are rejected. Do not store long-lived refresh tokens in browser local storage. Secure `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` BFF cookies are an optional source-supported alternative, not a selected architecture. Login/logout routes, session durations, refresh and expiry displays are **Needs confirmation**. [Source: p.21 §5.1; `screen_functions:r1:c30:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c30:f5`]
normalized_proposition_en: Access tokens contain issuer, audience, expiry, subject and tenant; unexpected algorithms and missing tenancy claims are rejected.

raw_quote_en: **Search:** Apply lexical and normalized vector retrieval, bounded candidates, reciprocal rank fusion, deterministic reranking, source diversity and per-query model-token budgets. Ranking is not authorization. Revoked source access must be effective **before next retrieval**, even while index cleanup is pending; source ACL changes invalidate affected cache before new results. Query fields, search placement, blank-query behavior, filtering and sorting remain open. If confidence/quality is insufficient, return `NO_SUPPORTED_EVIDENCE`, not fabricated context; clarification versus human routing needs a decision. Missing-citation generation has needs-review **or** unsupported outcome under TST-009, not a selected universal state. Approval binds exactly reviewed content. Final-response pointer and satisfied gate commit atomically; replay cannot publish another artifact under old approval. section_context_en: API-001 — Scope, authority and traceability
raw_quote_en: The API scope includes enterprise document ingestion, permission-aware retrieval, grounded drafting, deterministic policy, human review, publication, audit and controlled operations. Physical automation, irreversible financial transactions, foundation-model fine-tuning, unrestricted browsing and agent cloud-administration permissions are **Out of scope**. section_context_en: API-002 — Shared authentication and authorization
raw_quote_en: Every request binds an authenticated principal and tenant. Authorization combines role, tenant, workspace membership, resource attributes, case sensitivity, originating document ACL, action and separation of duties. Apply it at edge, domain transaction, retrieval, tool dispatch and publication as applicable. Navigation hiding is not authorization. Baseline roles are `Analyst`, `Reviewer`, `Admin`, `Auditor`, `Service`; Appendix A's `Owner`, `Member` and `approver` scopes require mapping. `Workspace Admin` is not silently equated with `Admin`. [Source: pp.11,21–23,41,83; `api:r1:c12:f1`, `api:r1:c29:f1`, `api:r1:c31:f1`, `api:r1:c31:f5`, `api:r1:c67:f1`, `api:r1:c137:f8`, `api:r1:c137:f15`]
normalized_proposition_en: Apply it at edge, domain transaction, retrieval, tool dispatch and publication as applicable.

section_context_en: DAT-016 — Audit, retention and controlled exit
raw_quote_en: Export/delete both require two independent approval checks and `Admin + approver` scope. Export explicitly requires **two-person approval plus manifest**; single Admin fails. Export contains case metadata, approved artifacts, source references and checksum audit manifests, excluding secrets/internal prompts. Deletion honors holds, writes tombstones, removes blobs/index entries and records receipts; held protected records are retained/receipted. Soft-deleted entities cannot be retrieved; final purge is scheduled tombstone processing. API-016/017 `202` is acceptance, not completion. Data-subject access uses the same inventory, not an invented endpoint. Tenant/workspace scope, partial receipts and lineage purge remain open. DAT-015 vault/rotation rules remain binding during retention/exit. Export contains case metadata, approved artifacts, source references and checksum audit manifests, excluding secrets/internal prompts. Deletion honors holds, writes tombstones, removes blobs/index entries and records receipts; held protected records are retained/receipted. Soft-deleted entities cannot be retrieved; final purge is scheduled tombstone processing. API-016/017 `202` is acceptance, not completion. Data-subject access uses the same inventory, not an invented endpoint. Tenant/workspace scope, partial receipts and lineage purge remain open. DAT-015 vault/rotation rules remain binding during retention/exit.
